newsitem.title: UK: Regulator says Railtrack must do better.
newsitem.headline: Regulator says Railtrack must do better.

text.p: British rail infrastructure operator Railtrack Group Plc is failing to invest adequately in the network and must take steps to renew the infrastructure, the Office of the Rail Regulator said on Thursday.
"Railtrack's record, in terms of its stewardship responsibilities, is disappointing in important aspects," regulator John Swift said in a statement.

Swift called on Railtrack to renew the railway infrastructure in a "timely fashion" and in the "appropriate modern form." He said Railtrack should develop the network to meed customers' needs, make good its current shortfall in expenditure and ensure its plans and investment approval processes delivered those objectives.

"The current level of underspend is totally unacceptable. Railtrack must demonstrate that it has credible plans to deal with that backlog and should deliver on those plans now it is free from public sector financing limits," Swift said.
Swift said Railtrack was due to deliver its Network Management Statement next month, which he said must detail plans for renewing the network and show significant progress in 1997.
Swift said he also expected Railtrack to promote services to passengers, ensure efficient train timetabling and operation, deliver better performance and promote rail freight.
